title: Adaptive Volumetric Mechanical Property Fields Invariant to Resolution
claim: One method produces detailed, accurate property fields across 3D representations, enabling realistic simulation in rich interactive scenes.
layout: Large scene left, arrow to 2 rows of results plus simulation strip
description: A large rendered living-room scene with a robot arm, sofa, pillows, TV and coffee table fills the left half. Orange arrows labeled Mesh and Gaussian Splat point to different parts of the scene, indicating the mixed 3D representations. A green block arrow labeled Adaptive VoMP leads to the right panel. The top row shows a sofa: the adaptive voxel structure as a wireframe, then Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio and density as colormapped point clouds, each with a colorbar. The middle row shows a GPU card with the same three property maps, plus a coarse VoMP baseline marked with a red X. The bottom strip shows three frames of a robot arm manipulating the GPU on a table. Colorful viridis maps catch the eye after the large scene.
caption: ADAVOMP generates high-resolution physically accurate volumetric mechanical property fields with detailed parts across 3D representations, enabling their use in building realistic interactive worlds and deformable simulations. We simulate a robot interacting with a high-resolution GPU and the sofa or pillows being stable under gravity in this Gaussian splat + mesh environment. ( : 01 :13)
abstract: Accurate mechanical properties (or materials) Young's modulus ($E$), Poisson's ratio ($Î½$) and density ($Ï$) are essential for reliable physics simulation of digital worlds, but most 3D assets lack this information. We propose AdaVoMP, a method for predicting accurate dense spatially-varying ($E$, $Î½$, $Ï$) for input 3D objects across representations, improving the resolution, accuracy, and memory efficiency over the state-of-the-art. The foundation of our technique is a sparse and adaptive voxel structure SAV that efficiently represents both the input 3D shape and the material field output. We replace the fixed-voxel model of the most accurate prior method, VoMP, with a novel sparse transformer encoder-decoder model that learns to generate a unique SAV autoregressively for every input shape to represent its materials, achieving a resolution $16^3\times$ higher than prior art. Experiments show that AdaVoMP estimates more accurate volumetric properties, even with lesser test-time compute than all prior art. This allows us to convert high-resolution complex 3D objects into simulation-ready assets, resulting in realistic deformable simulations.
